# Generate the C# API reference

This tool renders the public and protected `Fluence.Wpf` surface from the compiled .NET 10 assembly and its compiler XML comments. It writes generated Markdown to the local `docs/api/` staging directory; import those pages into the separate [website repository](https://github.com/sintaxasn/Fluence.Wpf.Website/tree/main/docs/api) for publication. The website can then build on Ubuntu without .NET or WPF.

From the repository root on Windows:

```powershell
dotnet build Fluence.Wpf/Fluence.Wpf.csproj -c Debug -f net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0
pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/ApiDocs/Generate-ApiDocs.ps1
pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/ApiDocs/Generate-ApiDocs.ps1 -Check
```

Use `-Configuration Release` if the library was built in Release. The `-Check` mode compares every generated byte with the checked-in pages and fails when any page differs. It does not edit files.

The generator excludes the generated XAML helper and internal types, displays declared public and protected members, and links inherited WPF behavior through the base type. [coverage.md](coverage.md) reports reflected member counts and missing compiler XML comments. The current missing comments are all on implicit parameterless constructors.

The generated pages use stable paths: `docs/api/<CLR namespace>/<type>.md`. Control guides can link to these pages without depending on heading anchors. Member anchors derive from compiler XML IDs, so adding an overload does not change existing anchors.
